title: Manickam–Singhi conjecture for vector spaces
statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, and let

$$
f:\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{1}_{q}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}
$$

be a weighting of the $1$-dimensional subspaces such that

$$
\sum_{v\in\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{1}_{q}}f(v)=0.
$$

For a subspace $S\subset V$, define its weight to be the sum of $f(v)$ over the $1$-dimensional subspaces $v\subset S$; call $S$ **nonnegative** if this weight is nonnegative. **Manickam–Singhi conjecture.** If $n\geq 4k$, then there are at least

$$
\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k-1}_{q}
$$

$k$-dimensional subspaces with nonnegative weight. The paper states that this vector-space analogue is resolved when $n\geq 3k$, whereas the conjecture remains open in its stated range $n\geq 4k$ only insofar as the source does not explicitly identify a resolution of that stronger range.
source_name: Ameera Chowdhury, Ghassan Sarkis and Shahriar Shahriari, “The Manickam-Miklós-Singhi Conjectures for Sets and Vector Spaces”, arXiv:1309.2212 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2212

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).
